text:
incident-bot: ALERT — p95/p99 latency regression detected for /v1/generate (region: us-west1). p95=1.82s (SLO 1.0s), p99=5.4s (SLO 2.5s). Streaming stall rate increased to 6.7% (baseline ~0.4%). Pager escalated to on-call. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/latency

simon: ack — I’m on it. is it global or a single region?

jane_sre: seeing same spike in us-west only, other regions look nominal. p95 heatmap shows a tight cluster of tail events around 14:06-14:12 UTC.

alex_prod: I rolled a minor model runner change ~13:58 UTC to the us-west pool (rate-limit batching tweak). Could be related, reverting now if needed.

maria_plat: checking autoscaler logs. no large scale-downs recently, pool size steady at 18 GPUs. CPU/mem fine. will pull worker logs.

simon: quick checklist: (1) any recent deploys? (2) autoscaler flapping? (3) network errors? (4) KV/cache backpressure?

alex_prod: deploy noted above; it was a config flip to batching windows (reduce max batch wait to 6ms). rolling restart completed at 13:59.

jane_sre: grabbing streaming worker logs now. pattern: many "stream stall: no-chunk-sent" entries from runner-24 and runner-25. latency spikes tied to those instances.

ops-bot: Runner health summary: runner-24 (gpu03) mem=83% gpu=93% temp=72C; runner-25 (gpu04) mem=79% gpu=89% temp=71C. Recent restart events: none.

simon: can we isolate those two runners from traffic? put them in maintenance to see if p95 improves.

maria_plat: isolating runner-24 & runner-25 from load balancer now: `redwoodctl pool drain --pool inference-usw1 --instances runner-24,runner-25`

simon: nice. also scale up the pool by +2 while we investigate.

maria_plat: scaling: `redwoodctl scale pool --pool inference-usw1 --replicas 20` — request accepted.

alex_prod: rolling back the batching change to previous value to rule out regressions. patch applied, restarting affected runners.

jane_sre: early telemetry: p95 dropped from 1.82s -> 0.95s within 90s of draining runners and scaling. p99 down to 2.9s. streaming stall rate down to 1.1%.

simon: good — seems the runners were the immediate cause. do we have root cause yet? logs showed kernel-level stalls on those GPUs?

maria_plat: kernel stack traces show sporadic driver timeouts (nvml) on runner-24 around 13:57. Could be flaky driver after the restart sequence. runner-25 shows similar but less severe.

alex_prod: the batching change triggered a small restart window for a subset of runners because of a config reload; maybe it exposed a driver bug under load.

jane_sre: customer impact estimate: between 13:58-14:08 UTC ~ 4.6k requests served from us-west. ~6.7% experienced streaming stalls; errors (timeoouts) ~0.8% (about 37 requests). Noting potential user-facing stalls but mostly degraded streaming latency.

simon: mitigation summary: (1) drained problematic runners, (2) scaled up pool, (3) rolled back batching config. monitoring will watch for recurrence.

ops-bot: Incident severity: SEV-2 (regional SLO breach). Incident channel: #incidents (this thread). Runbook link: https://wiki.redwood.internal/ops/runbooks/latency-regression

jane_sre: immediate next actions: collect full nvml logs from runner-24/25, open ticket with infra driver team, and schedule a controlled repro on a staging runner.

alex_prod: I’ll prepare the exact config diff and timeline and add to the ticket.

maria_plat: exporting logs: `redwoodctl logs fetch --instances runner-24,runner-25 --since 13:50 --output s3://redwood-incident-logs/1763900000/`

simon: customer comms: ops will create a short incident note. cc: support to triage any escalations.

jane_sre: support note draft: "We observed elevated streaming latency and intermittent stalls in us-west from 13:58–14:08 UTC affecting a subset of requests. Service has been stabilized; we are investigating runner driver issues and will follow up with root cause and mitigation."

simon: handoff to jane (next on-call) in 12m. I'll stay for the handoff window and then switch to watch only.

jane_sre: ack — I’m taking over monitoring and follow-ups. checklist on handoff: recent actions, logs exported, ticket created (INFRA-7821), scaling / rollback performed.

incident-bot: NOTE: Handoff recorded — from simon to jane_sre at 1763900720.

jane_sre: continuing monitoring — dashboards show steady p95 ~0.9s, p99 ~2.7s, stream stall ~0.9%. keeping page open for 30m then postmortem.

simon: thanks team. if we see recurrence, enable temporary routing to fallback-model-small via policy: `routing set --route /v1/generate --model fallback-small --priority 5`

ops-bot: support ticket created: SUP-4559, summary attached to incident.

jane_sre: noted. adding mitigation items to incident timeline and will kick off RCA doc. leaving the thread open — will update with root cause and remediation plan. :white_check_mark:
